title: The two parsers still disagree on four or more emphasis markers
foundBy: session agent, while fixing the three-marker case in CUI-015
details: `****four****` renders as `**four**` through the lightweight parser and as `four` through the rich one. CUI-015 fixed the three-marker case and stopped there on purpose. Runs of four or more are where CommonMark's delimiter matching stops being a scan and becomes a stack of openers and closers with rules about their lengths. Implementing a guess would trade a known disagreement for a less obvious one. Filed because MarkdownViewer.conformance.test.tsx asserts the two parsers produce the same DOM, and for this input that is still untrue. The corpus does not contain such a run, so the assertion passes. Either implement the run matching properly, or write down that the lightweight subset stops at three and say so where the conformance claim is made.

notes.text: Measured while verifying CUI-015: three markers match in both parsers, four do not.
